findings.premise: HLD §3/§'Processing...' claims 'the insrc model adapter uses the host's shared provider scheduling policy so the package does not introduce a second uncontrolled model lane' — i.e. a reusable runtime scheduling mechanism already exists in insrc that the new package's adapter can plug into to avoid overlapping model calls.
findings.evidence: The only daemon-wide model-selection mechanism found is RoleRouter (src/analyze/context/role-router.ts, resolveRole/createRoleRouter) and the config-driven tier table documented in docs/daemon.md §Model tiering — both select WHICH model/tier serves a role, with no concurrency/serialization logic. Grep across src/agent/providers and the daemon for a scheduler/semaphore/model-lane construct (`class.*Scheduler`, `Semaphore`, `modelLane`, `serialize.*model`) returned no matches outside unrelated LMDB-lock-guard files. The actual 'no overlapping model calls' guarantee in this codebase is a manual coding convention (CLAUDE.md: 'Never Promise.all anything that reaches an LLM provider ... always serial for...of') enforced by review discipline, not a pluggable runtime policy the new package could consume. [files: src/analyze/context/role-router.ts, docs/daemon.md, CLAUDE.md]
findings.action: Correct the HLD/owning LLD (s7, sc8) to state plainly that no shared concurrency-scheduling component exists today — only per-role model *selection* (RoleRouter) and a manual serial-await convention. The s7 LLD must design how the memory worker's model calls and the daemon's own model calls stay non-overlapping (e.g. its own internal serialization plus continued adherence to the serial-await convention), rather than assuming an existing 'host scheduling policy' it can delegate to.

findings.premise: sc2's `MemoryFailure.code` enum and `OperationState`/`OperationReceipt.errorCode` together cover the failure classes enumerated in the requirements doc's §15 Failure and crash-recovery table (backpressure, second writer, store unavailable/overflow, retrieval unavailable, worker-retry/quarantine), rather than leaving a named failure class with no detectable/handleable path.
findings.evidence: docs/reqs/shared-project-memory.html §15's rows map cleanly onto HLD sc2's codes: 'Queue capacity exhausted'->BACKPRESSURE, 'Second writer / ownership'->OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT, 'Retrieval/index unavailable'->STORE_UNAVAILABLE/CONTEXT_OVERFLOW, stale correction->REVISION_CONFLICT, and asynchronous worker outcomes (malformed output, repeated model failure) are carried via `OperationReceipt.state` ('failed'|'quarantined') + `errorCode` rather than the synchronous `MemoryFailure` enum — a defensible split between call-time and processing-time failure reporting that the HLD's §'Admission and queue contract' and §'Processing...' sections describe consistently.
findings.action: none — verified sound; note for the owning LLD (s1/s2) to keep this call-time-vs-processing-time error-reporting split explicit so it isn't collapsed into one enum later
